question: Which of the following is a correct representation of a compound formed by ionic bonding?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NaCl**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ionic Bonding:** Ionic bonding occurs when atoms transfer electrons to achieve stability. In this type of bond, one atom donates electrons, becoming a positively charged **cation**, while the other atom accepts electrons, becoming a negatively charged **anion**. The electrostatic attraction between these oppositely charged ions forms the bond.
 
• **NaCl (Sodium Chloride):** Sodium chloride is a classic example of a compound formed by ionic bonding. In NaCl, **sodium (Na)** donates one electron to achieve a stable electronic configuration, forming a positive ion (Na⁺). Meanwhile, **chlorine (Cl)** accepts the electron to complete its octet, forming a negative ion (Cl⁻). The electrostatic attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions results in the ionic bond.
 
• Compounds like **NaCl** typically have a crystalline structure due to the arrangement of ions in a lattice format. These compounds exhibit high melting and boiling points and conduct electricity in molten or aqueous states. *Hence, NaCl is correct.*
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **H₂O:** Water is a covalent compound, not ionic. It forms through sharing of electrons between hydrogen and oxygen atoms. *Hence, incorrect.*
 
• **CO₂:** Carbon dioxide is also a covalent compound formed by sharing electrons between carbon and oxygen atoms. *Hence, incorrect.*
 
• **NH₃:** Ammonia is another example of a covalent compound formed by sharing electrons between nitrogen and hydrogen atoms. *Hence, incorrect.*
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is NaCl.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Ionic Compounds:**

 
 
• **High melting and boiling points:** Due to strong electrostatic forces between ions, ionic compounds require significant energy to break the bonds.
 
• **Electrical conductivity:** Ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten or aqueous states as ions are free to move.
 
• **Solubility:** Ionic compounds are generally soluble in polar solvents like water.
 
• **Crystalline structure:** Ionic compounds form well-defined crystals due to the orderly arrangement of ions.
 
 
 
• **Applications of NaCl:**
 
 
• **Common salt:** NaCl is widely used as table salt in culinary practices.
 
• **Industrial use:** It serves as a raw material in the production of chemicals like sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and chlorine gas (Cl₂).
 
• **De-icing:** NaCl is used to melt ice on roads during winter.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Ionic and Covalent Bonds:**

 
 
• **Ionic bonds:** Formed by the transfer of electrons, leading to the creation of charged ions.
 
• **Covalent bonds:** Formed by sharing electrons between atoms.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Ionic Compounds:**
 
 
• Common examples include **NaCl (sodium chloride)**, **MgO (magnesium oxide)**, and **CaF₂ (calcium fluoride)**.
